title: Best Dehumidifier with Pump (2026): Self-Draining Picks
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers with a Built-In Pump
dek: Stop carrying sloshing buckets up the basement stairs. A built-in pump pushes the water up and out, so the machine runs for weeks without you.
description: The best dehumidifier with pump for basements and crawl spaces: built-in pump models from hOmeLabs, Frigidaire, Honeywell, Waykar and AlorAir, compared.
intro: A bucket is fine in a room you walk through every day. In a basement or crawl space, emptying a full tank twice a day gets old fast — and the day you forget, the unit shuts off and the damp creeps back. A **dehumidifier with a pump** fixes that for good: its built-in condensate pump pushes collected water *upward*, through a thin hose to a window well, laundry sink or drain, so the machine can run unattended for weeks.

That one feature separates a dehumidifier you babysit from one you forget about. But pump lift heights, coverage claims and model numbers vary a lot, and several brands sell near-identical units with and without pumps. We sorted out which self-draining models are worth buying and which one suits your space.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers with pumps

blocks.text: We don't run pump-lift trials in a test basement. We compare capacity under the 2019 DOE test (and flag brands whose marketing names overstate it), pump lift and hose length from manuals, ENERGY STAR listings, minimum operating temperatures and the CPSC recall database.

Pumps are the part most likely to cause trouble, so owner reviews carry extra weight here. We looked for recurring reports of pumps that stop lifting, error codes tied to clogged screens and hoses that pop off, and favored designs with a solid track record.

sections.heading: What to look for in a dehumidifier with a built-in pump

items.label: Enough lift for your route
items.text: Measure the vertical distance from the unit to your window, sink or drain. It must be less than the pump's rated lift, with some margin for a long hose run.

items.label: A real pump, not just a hose port
items.text: Many listings mention continuous drainage but only have a gravity outlet. Look for the words "built-in pump." If you have a floor drain, a [drain-hose model](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-drain-hose/) may be all you need.

items.label: Easy-to-clean pump screen
items.text: A clogged intake screen is the most common failure. A quick monthly rinse keeps it working.

items.label: Auto-restart and defrost
items.text: A pump unit runs unattended, so it should resume after an outage and keep working in a cool basement.

items.label: The right capacity
items.text: A 50-pint unit suits most basements and large rooms. For crawl spaces and permanent installs, step up to a commercial unit.

sections.heading: Dehumidifier pump options: built-in vs. add-on condensate pump

blocks.text: Already own a good dehumidifier without a pump? You don't necessarily need a new one. A standalone **condensate pump** — the small reservoir-and-pump units sold for furnaces and air conditioners — can sit next to the dehumidifier and collect water from its gravity-drain hose, then push it up and out.

items: **Built-in pump:** neatest setup and one power cord, but if the pump fails, the whole unit may need service.

**Add-on condensate pump:** works with any dehumidifier that has a gravity outlet, and it's cheap to replace. It does add a second device, a second plug and a small reservoir that needs occasional cleaning.
**Either way:** route the hose so it can't kink, secure it at the discharge end and check it monthly.

blocks.title: Pump not lifting?
blocks.text: Rinse the pump's intake screen, check the hose for kinks or an air lock, and make sure the discharge point isn't higher than the rated lift. Our [dehumidifier not working guide](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) covers pump error codes.

The **hOmeLabs HME1003 Wi-Fi** is the best dehumidifier with a pump for most homes. Choose the **Waykar** for the widest coverage, the **Frigidaire FHDP5033W1** for Wi-Fi scheduling and a living-space noise level, the **Honeywell TPFIT50PWK** for big open rooms, and the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S** when water has to climb out of a crawl space. Route the hose to a drain, set the humidistat around 50% and you'll never carry a bucket again.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier with a pump?
faqs.a: The hOmeLabs HME1003 Wi-Fi for most homes. It's a 50-pint unit with high airflow and a built-in pump that pushes water to a sink or window, suitable for large basements. For crawl spaces, the AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S's 19.6-ft pump lift is the stronger choice.

faqs.q: Why buy a dehumidifier with a pump instead of a drain hose?
faqs.a: A gravity hose only works if a floor drain or sump sits lower than the unit. A pump lifts water upward — to a window, laundry sink or overhead drain — so you can put the dehumidifier wherever it's needed.

faqs.q: How high can a dehumidifier pump lift water?
faqs.a: Portable units typically lift roughly 12–16 feet, while commercial crawl-space units like the AlorAir HDi65S reach about 19.6 feet. Check the rated lift against your actual route before buying.

faqs.q: Can I add a condensate pump to a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Yes. If your dehumidifier has a gravity-drain outlet, you can run its hose into a standalone condensate pump, which then pushes the water up and out. It's a cheap way to add self-draining to a unit you already own.

faqs.q: Does GE or Frigidaire make a dehumidifier with a pump?
faqs.a: Both do. Frigidaire's pump models include the FHDP5033W1 and the FFAP5033W1, and GE sells pump versions such as the APER50LZ. Compare them in our [GE dehumidifier guide](/best/best-ge-dehumidifier/) and Frigidaire guide.

faqs.q: Is a heat pump dehumidifier the same as a dehumidifier with a pump?
faqs.a: No. "Heat pump dehumidifier" describes how a compressor dehumidifier works — it moves heat from a cold coil to a warm one — and applies to almost every refrigerant model. A dehumidifier with a pump has an extra water pump for drainage.

faqs.q: Are dehumidifiers with pumps less reliable?
faqs.a: The pump is one more part that can fail, so choose a reputable brand and rinse the intake screen regularly. If your layout allows gravity drainage, a non-pump unit has fewer moving parts.
